newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Bancomer downgraded from buy.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Bancomer downgraded from buy.

text.p: Mexican brokerage Finamex said Monday it downgraded Mexico's second-largest financial firm Grupo Financiero Bancomer (GFB) to market performer from buy after reviewing 1997 and 1998 estimates under new accounting rules.

"At a price of 3.50 pesos per "B" share, GFB trades at 26.3 times 1997 estimated earnings or 21.3 times adjusted 1997 estimated earnings (excluding monetary gains and losses of Bancomer)," analyst Rogelio Urrutia said.

"We believe that at this level, the share prices recognises the sound asset quality of the bank and its relatively healthier position amongs its peers. GFB shares have outperformed a strong Bolsa index by 13.9 percentage points in the last 30 days," he added.
Urrutia said Bancomer's 1997 results will be negatively impacted by the new accounting rules. "Net interest income will decline by 19 percent according to our estimates," he said.
Mexican banks can no longer recognize as interest income any accrued interest arising from its past-due loans, as was common practice under the old rule, he added.

Urrutia said other factors to deter net interest income will be low credit demand, the decline in lending rates, the change in the mix to less productive assets and Bancomer's continuous efforts to maintain its market share in branch deposits.
